title: Only the sky
translation: A hermit called something or other once said: "Nothing ties me down anymore. The only thing I'll be sorry to leave is the sky." I can really see that.
original: {某|なにがし}とかやいひし{世|よ}すて{人|びと}の、この{世|よ}のほだしもたらぬ{身|み}に、ただ{空|そら}のなごりのみぞ{惜|を}しき。」といひしこそ、まことにさも{覚|おぼ}えぬべけれ。
literal: That a world-renouncer called something or other said, 'For me, who has none of the fetters of this world, only the lingering (beauty) of the sky is hard to part with': truly, one can surely feel so.

notes.text: 'Someone called something or other': Kenkō does not remember the name, or does not care. Compare Shida-something in section 236.
ほだし: 'fetters', the ties that keep a person in the world: family, possessions, duties. A hermit who has cut them all is free to go, and this one finds he still has one tie: the sky.

notes.quote: 空のなごりのみぞ惜しき
notes.text: なごり: what lingers after something is gone, and the sadness of parting. ぞ … き: ぞ needs the attributive form, so {惜|を}し becomes {惜|を}しき. The 1925 edition has a closing quotation mark here but no opening one.
